extracted.intended_audience: players of daily word/grouping puzzles (e.g., NYT Connections) and wordplay enthusiasts
extracted.subtask_description: Daily 'Connections' style word puzzles where 16 words (or short phrases/emojis) must be sorted into four color-coded groups of four that share a common category or relation. Each puzzle is published with a date and puzzle number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Color-coded groups (Yellow / Green / Blue / Purple)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each puzzle is presented as four color-labelled groups: Yellow Group, Green Group, Blue Group, Purple Group. Under each color heading are four entries (words, short phrases, or emoji) representing the members of that group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example headings from the page: 'Yellow Group:', 'Green Group:', 'Blue Group:', 'Purple Group:'. Example group entries: 'Yellow Group: CAKE, COAT, PLASTER, SMEAR' and 'Blue Group: BAR, BUBBLE, LINE, PIE'. The color labels partition the puzzle's 16 items into four answer clusters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group membership: four related items
rubrics_metrics.description: Each color group contains exactly four items that share a common semantic or surface relation (a category, type, pattern, or wordplay connection).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of relations from the page: 'MUSIC GENRES: BLUES, COUNTRY, FOLK, ROCK' (category = music genres); 'HOMOPHONES: TO, TOO, TUE, TWO' (phonetic relation); 'STARTING WITH PIXAR MOVIES: COCONUT, SOULMATE, UPDO, WALLET' (prefix/pattern relation). Items may be single words, multiword phrases (e.g., 'MAKE OUT'), or emoji (e.g., April 1 entries).

rubrics_metrics.name: Variety of category types allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: Categories are not limited to simple 'kinds of X' — they include synonyms, antonyms, homophones, items that 'start with' or 'end with' particular letters/words, proper nouns, abbreviations, clued phrases, and other wordplay patterns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observed category types on this page include: 'KINDS OF CHARTS', 'ZODIAC SYMBOLS', 'DR. SEUSS TITLE FIGURES', 'STARTS OF U.S. PRESIDENTS', 'SILENT “T”', 'U.S. STATE ABBREVIATIONS', 'WORDS ENDING IN NUMBERS', 'NATO PHONETIC ALPHABET', 'HORROR MOVIES, WITH “THE”', 'HOMOPHONES OF MUSICALS'. Many puzzles mix literal categories (e.g., 'TREES') with linguistic patterns (e.g., 'SILENT “K”').

rubrics_metrics.name: Puzzle metadata: date and puzzle number
rubrics_metrics.description: Each puzzle listing is labeled with a publication date and a puzzle number (e.g., 'August 20, 2024, #436'), which identifies the daily puzzle instance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page shows a chronological archive; use the date/# to reference or file puzzles. Example: 'July 15, 2024, #400'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Answer item forms and permissive surface variants
rubrics_metrics.description: Answer items can appear as single words, multiword phrases, hyphenated forms, abbreviations, or even emojis; capitalization/formatting varies (ALL CAPS in this archive).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: multiword entries like 'MERRY-GO-ROUND', 'MAKE OUT', abbreviations like 'HI, MA, OR, PA' (U.S. state abbreviations), emoji entries on April 1 ('🥓, 🍞, 🥬, 🧀'), and items that are proper nouns (e.g., 'BLAH' examples). Puzzles may also include items that are clued indirectly (e.g., 'STARTS OF U.S. PRESIDENTS: BIDE, CART, NIX, WASHING' where entries are letter sequences rather than full names).
